english.title: Aggravated vehicle taking - (initial taker) and property damage under £5000
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority, took a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), for the use of yourself or another, and after the vehicle was unlawfully taken and before it was recovered, owing to the driving of the vehicle, an accident occurred by which damage of less than £5000 was caused to property other than the vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..).

(A)_[There were no other additional aggravating factors]_
(B)_[Additional aggravating factors were **(..SPECIFY THE FACTORS..)]_

english.notes:
(i) This wording is for use only were the defendant was the 'initial taker' - for a 'subsequent driver' see H4483 and 'being carried on' see H4486.
(ii) See also H4383, H4382, H4391, H4481 and H4482 for other aggravated vehicle taking wordings relating to the 'initial taker'.
(iii) This offence wording should only be used for damage under five thousand pounds.
(iv) See offence wordings: H4384 for damage over five thousand pounds.
(v) This is an either way offence but triable summarily because the only aggravating feature is damage below £5000 (but see section 40 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988).
(vi) Offences under section 12A are generally punishable on conviction on indictment by up to two years’ imprisonment except where the offence alleges only damage valued at less than £5,000 as the aggravating element in which case the maximum penalty is six months (as per sections 22 and 33(3) of, and Schedule 2 to, the Magistrates Court Act 1980).

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Obligatory disqualification - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

There is no time limit on prosecution for this offence - even though triable summarily this remains an either way offence.
